old_caption: The video captures a serene outdoor scene featuring a xylophone placed on a light-colored wooden surface. Surrounding the xylophone are numerous colorful marbles scattered across the table. The xylophone itself has keys in various bright colors, including red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple, each adorned with small metallic balls at the ends. The background reveals a concrete wall and some dry grass, suggesting a garden or backyard setting. The lighting is natural, indicating daytime, with shadows cast by nearby trees adding depth to the scene. Throughout the video, the marbles roll around the xylophone, occasionally bumping into it, creating a dynamic yet peaceful atmosphere. There are no visible characters or animals in the frame, focusing entirely on the interaction between the marbles and the xylophone. The camera remains stationary, providing a clear and steady view of the entire setup.

caption: The video captures an outdoor tabletop scene where a wooden xylophone with eight colored metal bars lies diagonally against a sun-dappled concrete wall, ringed by scattered glossy marbles. At the right edge, angled tube chutes release marbles that roll along the back edge of the instrument, and this motion is already underway. A red marble leaves the tube mouth and travels steadily leftward along the rear rail, easing toward the middle bars. Behind it, a white marble emerges from the chute and drifts along the same back edge. A small magenta marble drifts leftward along the back rail, and a second magenta marble emerges near the tube mouth. The marbles resting on the colored bars hold their places with only minor jitter, whereas the loose marbles on the open table shift in slow rolling motion. The framing itself drifts, sliding the tubes partly toward the right edge. Throughout, marbles continue to rest and roll along the colorful bars.

draft_caption: The video captures an outdoor tabletop scene where a wooden xylophone with eight colored metal bars lies diagonally against a sun-dappled concrete wall, ringed by scattered glossy marbles. At the right edge, angled tube chutes feed marbles onto the instrument, and a rolling process is already underway. A red marble leaves the tube mouth and travels steadily leftward, hopping across the bars toward the middle and left keys. Behind it, a white marble emerges from the chute and follows the same path, settling onto the orange and yellow bars. A small magenta marble drifts left along the back rail and levels out. Marbles already resting on the bars creep gradually leftward, while the loose marbles on the open table shift in slow rolling motion. The framing itself drifts, sliding the tubes partly out of view at the right. Throughout, marbles continue to rest and roll along the colorful bars.
